name: Hag’s Glen

attributes.attribute: sacred site in Munster in southwest Ireland
also called Coom Callee, part of MacGillycuddy's Reeks, the highest Irish mountains

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Hag's Glen, also called Coom Callee, is a sacred site in southwest Ireland. It lies in the province of Munster. The glen forms part of MacGuillycuddy's Reeks, the highest mountains in Ireland. Legend ties the valley to the Cailleach, the powerful figure of the hag. A local tale says a hag in that glen cared for a small child, and a rock was imprinted with their footprints. In the mid-nineteenth century an old woman who lived alone in the Glen took the name of the Cailleach, strengthening the link between the valley and the mythological hag.

okr.objective: Document Hag's Glen as the Munster valley sacred to the Cailleach.
